content:
The Goedel team is happy to annouce our open sourced SOTA model Goedel-Prover-V2.

Our flagship model, Goedel-Prover-V2-32B, achieves the new SOTA:

  • It achieves 88.0% on MiniF2F at Pass@32 on standard mode and 90.4% on self-correction mode, outperforming prior SOTA DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B by a large margin (nearly 6-8%).
  • The model in self-correction mode solves 64 problems on PutnamBench at only Pass@64, securing the 1st on the leaderboard surpassing DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B's record of solving 47 problems by Pass@1024.
  • Our model solves 73 vs 50 over 671B DeepSeek Prover on MathOlympiadBench  by Pass@32. MathOlympiadBench (Math Olympiad Bench) comprises human-verified formalizations of IMO-level mathematical competition problems, sourced from Compfiles and IMOSLLean4 repository.

Our small model, Goedel-Prover-V2-8B, reaches 83.3% on MiniF2F test set at Pass@32, matching the performance of prior state-of-the-art DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B while being nearly 100 times smaller in model size.

Built on the standard expert iteration and reinforcement learning pipeline, our approach incorporates three key innovations:
(1) Scaffolded data synthesis: We generate synthetic proof tasks of increasing difficulty to progressively train the model, enabling it to master increasingly complex theorems;
(2) Verifier-guided self-correction: The model learns to iteratively revise its own proofs by leveraging feedback from Lean’s compiler, closely mimicking how humans refine their work;
(3) Model averaging: We combine multiple model checkpoints to improve robustness and overall performance.

Checkout our Blog and model on Huggingface.
